Learning outcomes
  1. Identify and combine like terms.
  2. Apply the distributive property to remove parentheses.
  3. Multiply two binomials using the FOIL method.
``` - Simplifying an expression means rewriting it in an equivalent, yet shorter form. - In the following sections, we will revisit some common methods used to simplify algebraic expressions. ## Addition and subtraction of like terms - A term consists of a variable (or variables) raised to a certain power and multiplied by a coefficient (a number). - For instance, in the term $3x^2 \Rightarrow$ $x$ is the variable, $3$ is the coefficient, and $2$ is the exponent. - Like terms have the same variable part raised to the same power, but their coefficients may differ (e.g., $2x$, $\displaystyle \frac{1}{3}x$, and $-2x$ are like terms). - To combine like terms, add or subtract their coefficients while keeping the variable part unchanged. - For example, $3x$, $-4x$, and $7x$ can be simplified as $3x-4x+7x=6x$. - Terms such as $5x$ and $3x^2$, or $8xy$ and $4x$, are not like terms and cannot be combined by addition or subtraction. ## Removing parentheses using the distributive property - The distributive property states that the product of a sum or difference $a(x \pm y)$ is equal to the sum or difference of the products ($ax \pm ay$). - Using this property, parentheses can be be removed by multiplying the term outside the parentheses by every term inside. ```{=html}
Worked Examples & Practice
``` ::: panel-tabset ## Example M.2.1 {{< iconify ic:round-menu-book size=21px >}} Simplify: $\displaystyle \boldsymbol {a (3+4a)}$ ![Distributive property](/images/parenth.png){fig-align="center" width="200"} $$a (3+4a) = 3a+4a^2$$ ## Example M.2.2 {{< iconify ic:round-menu-book size=21px >}} Simplify: $\displaystyle \boldsymbol {5b-b(2+7b)}$ $$ \begin{aligned} 5b-b(2+7b) &=5b+(-b)(2+7b)\\ &=5b-2b-7b^2\\ &=(5b-2b)-7b^2\\ &=\boxed{3b-7b^2} \end{aligned} $$ ## [Exercise M.2.1 {{< iconify fluent:chat-bubbles-question-20-filled size=21px >}}]{style="color: #ba181b"} Simplify: $\displaystyle \boldsymbol{\frac{1}{2}(2c-8)}$ The answer is ::: ## Multiplication of two binomials ### Binomials {#binomials} - A binomial is a [polynomial](003_factorization.qmd#polynomial) that has exactly two non-zero, unlike terms. - A binomial in one variable can be expressed as: $$ ax^m+bx^n $$ **where**: - $\displaystyle x$ is the variable. - $\displaystyle a$ and $\displaystyle b$ are non-zero coefficients that can take any [real number ](#real-numbers). - $\displaystyle m$ and $\displaystyle n$ are distinct exponents. - the two terms, $\displaystyle ax^m$ and $\displaystyle bx^n$, are unlike terms. ::: {.callout-note title="Real numbers ($\\mathbb{R}$)" #real-numbers} - Real numbers include all rational and irrational numbers: - **Rational numbers** are numbers that can be written as a ratio of two integers $\displaystyle \frac{a}{b}$, where $\displaystyle b \ne 0$ (e.g., $\displaystyle \frac{1}{4}$). Their decimal expansions either terminate (e.g., $\displaystyle \frac{1}{4} = 0.25$) or repeat (e.g., $\displaystyle \frac{1}{3} = 0.333... = 0.\overline{3}$). - Integers (e.g., $-3$, $0$, and $5$) are a subset of rational numbers, where the denominator $\displaystyle b = 1$ (i.e., $\displaystyle -3 = \frac{-3}{1}$). - **Irrational numbers** are numbers that cannot be expressed as a ratio of two integers (e.g., $\displaystyle \sqrt{2}$ and $\displaystyle \pi$). The decimal expansion of an irrational number does not terminate nor repeat. For example, $\displaystyle \pi \approx 3.14159265358979323846...$, its decimal expansion does not repeat nor terminate. Although $\pi$ is approximated as $3.14$ or $\displaystyle \frac{22}{7}$, these are not exact values. ::: ### How to multiply two binomials - Multiplying two binomials is an application of the distributive property, where each term in the first binomial is multiplied by each term in the second binomial, and then any like terms are combined. - This process can be remembered using the mnemonic **FOIL** (@fig-foil), which stands for: - **F – First**: Multiply the first terms in each binomial ($\displaystyle a \times c$). - **O – Outer**: Multiply the outer terms in each binomial ($\displaystyle a \times d$). - **I – Inner**: Multiply the inner terms in each binomial ($\displaystyle b \times c$). - **L – Last**: Multiply the last terms in each binomial ($\displaystyle b \times d$). ![FOIL method for multiplying binomials](/images/FOIL3.png){#fig-foil fig-align="center" width="400"} ```{=html}
Worked Examples & Practice
``` ::: panel-tabset ## Example M.2.3 {{< iconify ic:round-menu-book size=21px >}} Simplify: $\displaystyle \boldsymbol {(x+5)(x-2)}$ $$ \begin{aligned} (x+5)(x-2) &=\underbrace{(x \times x)}_{\text{First}} + \underbrace{(x \times -2)}_{\text{Outer}} + \underbrace{(5 \times x)}_{\text{Inner}} + \underbrace{(5 \times -2)}_{\text{Last}}\\ &=x^2 -2x + 5x -10\\ &=\boxed{x^2 + 3x -10} \end{aligned} $$ ## Example M.2.4 {{< iconify ic:round-menu-book size=21px >}} Simplify: $\displaystyle \boldsymbol{(y^2-4y)(3-y)}$ $$ \begin{aligned} (y^2-4y)(3-y) &=\underbrace{(y^2 \times 3)}_{\text{First}} + \underbrace{(y^2 \times -y)}_{\text{Outer}} + \underbrace{(-4y \times 3)}_{\text{Inner}} + \underbrace{(-4y \times -y)}_{\text{Last}}\\ &=3y^2 - y^3 - 12y + 4y^2\\ &=\boxed{-y^3+7y^2-12y} \end{aligned} $$ ## [Exercise M.2.2 {{< iconify fluent:chat-bubbles-question-20-filled size=21px >}}]{style="color: #ba181b"} Simplify: $\displaystyle \boldsymbol{(3x^2-4y)(2x+5y)}$
$$ \begin{aligned} (3x^2-4y)(2x+5y) &=\underbrace{(3x^2 \times 2x)}_{\text{First}} +\underbrace{(3x^2 \times 5y)}_{\text{Outer}} +\underbrace{(-4y \times 2x)}_{\text{Inner}} +\underbrace{(-4y \times 5y)}_{\text{Last}}\\ &=\boxed{6x^3+15x^2y-8xy-20y^2} \end{aligned} $$
